headline: SQD disaggregates subquadratic-attention inference around heterogeneous memory and compute regimes
summary: SQD (SubQuadratic Disaggregation) argues that serving systems designed around dense-attention assumptions leave efficiency on the table for sparse, linear and sliding-window attention models. It splits decode according to which subquadratic components require full-KV indexing versus static-memory compute, then maps those components onto heterogeneous DRAM/SRAM resources. In the authors' adjusted 8xB200 system proxy, reported average tokens/J gains over their strongest GPU-only baselines are 53% on GLM 5.2, 31% on Nemotron 3 Ultra and 56% on Gemma 4 31B. An analytical Rubin+LPX fixed-power model reports 1.2x-1.5x tighter achievable latency and up to 3.6x throughput versus attention-FFN disaggregation.
